title: Multifamily Replacement Sourcing
name: Multifamily Replacement Sourcing
metaTitle: Multifamily Replacement Sourcing in Dallas, TX
metaDescription: Multifamily 1031 replacement sourcing across Dallas: garden-style and mid-rise stock, rent roll review, and identification-window coordination.

sections.html:
Multifamily is the asset class most exchange investors ask about first, and it's also the one where a bad rent roll hides the longest. Dallas has enough apartment stock in enough different price points that a real candidate list is possible inside the 45-day window, but only if someone is pulling trailing financials the day the search starts, rather than the day an offer gets written.

The urgency is real: strong garden-style product in the right submarket can go under contract to someone else within days of hitting the market, so the sourcing effort has to be moving before the relinquished sale even reaches the closing table.

sections.heading: Where Apartment Stock Splits by Era and Rent Level
sections.html:
Uptown and the area around Knox-Henderson carry newer mid-rise product built for renters paying a premium for walkability, with amenity packages and staffing costs that change the operating expense line significantly. East Dallas and the Lake Highlands corridor carry an older garden-style stock, much of it built in the 1970s and 1980s, where the upside is usually interior renovation rather than rent growth from new supply.

Further out toward Garland and Mesquite, garden-style complexes trade at a lower basis per unit, which matters for an investor exchanging out of a smaller relinquished property who needs the numbers to pencil without over-leveraging.

sections.heading: Why Out-of-State Exchange Money Keeps Landing Here
sections.html:
A meaningful share of the multifamily buyers we work with are exchanging out of California or the Northeast, and Texas having no state income tax changes the after-tax cash flow math on top of whatever cap rate they're buying at. That inbound demand is part of why decent garden-style product doesn't sit on the market long, and why a candidate list assembled too late tends to be full of properties that are already under contract to someone else.

For an investor coming from a high-tax state, the appeal goes beyond the purchase price relative to what they sold: it's the difference in what actually reaches their pocket each year once state income tax stops being part of the equation, which changes how aggressively they're willing to bid on a solid Dallas property.

sections.heading: Reading the Rent Roll Before It Reaches Your List
sections.html: We pull unit mix, loss-to-lease, and delinquency trend before anything gets added to a client's identification letter. A property showing rent growth on paper that's really just new leases masking flat renewals on long-term tenants gets flagged, because that gap becomes the buyer's problem the day escrow closes.

sections.heading: What We Check Against Every Multifamily Candidate
sections.html:
Every property on a candidate list gets run through the same checklist before it's presented, and the pro forma alone never clears it on its own:

  • Trailing twelve months of collections against posted rents
  • Deferred maintenance on roofs, HVAC, and foundations across the unit count
  • Property tax reassessment risk tied to the sale price
  • Renovation capital already spent versus what's left to complete a value-add plan
  • Utility billback structure and whether residents are separately metered

That last item catches more surprises than people expect, since a property billing utilities back to residents shows a very different expense line than one where the owner absorbs water and trash costs directly.

sections.heading: Keeping the Purchase on Schedule for the QI
sections.html:
Apartment deals often carry loan assumption or new-debt underwriting that runs long, so we build the purchase timeline backward from your 180-day exchange period rather than forward from when an offer gets accepted. Funds route through your qualified intermediary at every step so you never take actual or constructive receipt of the exchange proceeds.

When a lender's assumption review is the long pole in the schedule, we push for that conversation to start the same week the property lands on the identification letter, not after the letter is already filed and the clock has less runway left.

faqs.q: What multifamily price points are realistic for a Dallas 1031 exchange?
faqs.a: It depends on the relinquished property size, but garden-style assets in East Dallas, Lake Highlands, Garland, and Mesquite give investors a wider range of entry prices than newer Uptown mid-rise product, which trades at a meaningfully higher basis per unit.

faqs.q: Why do so many multifamily buyers here come from other states?
faqs.a: Texas has no state income tax, which improves after-tax cash flow relative to states like California or New York. That inbound exchange demand is a real factor in how quickly decent product moves off market.

faqs.q: How do you catch a rent roll that's been dressed up for a sale?
faqs.a: We compare trailing collections to posted rents and look for renewal leases priced flat while new move-in leases show growth. That gap usually means the pro forma is optimistic rather than the asset actually performing.

faqs.q: Does a multifamily property need to be professionally managed to qualify as replacement property?
faqs.a: No. Self-managed properties qualify the same as third-party managed ones for like-kind purposes. Management structure affects underwriting and your own workload, not the exchange itself, though it's worth discussing early since it shapes what kind of property fits your capacity.

faqs.q: Can loan assumption delay a multifamily replacement closing past the 180-day exchange period?
faqs.a: It can if it's not planned for early. We build the purchase and financing timeline backward from your 180-day deadline so a lender's assumption review doesn't become the reason a closing slips past the window, and we flag any assumption requirement the day a candidate is identified.
